text: Deadlines are a part of everyday work and study, and managing them well is a valuable skill. The key is effective time management. Instead of seeing a deadline as a distant threat, break your project into smaller tasks and schedule them over the available days. Prioritization is also essential; focus on the most complex or important parts first, when your energy is highest. Furthermore, practice scope management. It’s common to want to add extra features or details, but this can make you miss your date. Learn to say “no” to unnecessary additions. Finally, keep communication open. If you foresee a problem, inform your team or teacher early. They may offer help or adjust the deadline, which is far better than silence and a missed delivery.
